resources.string: LocationManager is unavailable: system_server did not start the location service.
LocationManager has no \"gps\" provider: the GNSS HAL (android.hardware.gnss) is not registered or crashed at boot. Check lshal and logcat for GnssLocationProvider and the vendor location daemons.
Turn on location (Quick Settings) and run again: the satellite checks are skipped while it is off.
The provider works but the ROM does not declare android.hardware.location.gps: copy android.hardware.location.gps.xml in the device tree, otherwise some apps hide GPS functions.
There is no GNSS engine to listen to; see the GPS provider result.
Detailed capabilities need Android 12 or later

Normal without Google Play services or microG with a location backend: apps that ask for network location get nothing, and indoors there is no position at all. Many apps then fall back to GPS only, which needs open sky.
registerGnssStatusCallback failed: the location service refused the request (permission or a broken GNSS HAL).
No status from the GNSS engine in %1$d s

The engine never reported satellites: the GNSS HAL does not start the receiver. On Qualcomm the engine runs on the modem: check the location daemons (loc_launcher, lowi), the GNSS HAL service and the modem firmware.
The engine runs but lists no satellite at all: no RF reaches it (antenna, LNA power) or the receiver is not started in the modem.
%1$d satellites seen (%2$s), up to %3$d used in fix
See the satellites result: nothing was received.
The receiver is not getting RF: the satellites come from almanac predictions and none is actually tracked. The antenna/LNA path or the RF configuration in the modem (RFC, external LNA enable) is off.

The receiver is not getting RF: the satellites come from almanac predictions and none is tracked; the NMEA GSV sentences carry no SNR either. The antenna/LNA path or the RF configuration in the modem (RFC, external LNA enable) is off.
NMEA GSV reports SNR up to %1$s dB-Hz but GnssStatus says 0: RF is fine, the GNSS HAL does not copy C/N0 into the framework report.
Max %1$s dB-Hz, mean %2$s dB-Hz on %3$d satellites
Very weak signal. Normal indoors; outdoors with open sky expect 30–45 dB-Hz. If it stays this low outside, check antenna contact, LNA gain and the RF calibration.
requestLocationUpdates on the GPS provider failed: permission, or the provider is missing or disabled.
No fix because no satellite signal is received: see the signal result.

Satellites are heard but there is no fix yet. Normal indoors: retry outside with open sky. A cold start without assistance data (XTRA/PSDS, no network) can take several minutes; use the live view to wait for the first fix.
Fix after %1$s s, accuracy %2$s m, %3$d satellites used
The GPS time is off by about 1024 weeks: GPS week-number rollover in the receiver firmware or HAL. Apps that trust GPS time get a date about 19.6 years off.
GPS time and system time differ by %1$d s: the system clock is wrong (no NTP or NITZ) or the HAL reports a wrong UTC time.
The fix is at 0°, 0°: the HAL reports a position without valid coordinates.
Accuracy worse than 500 m for a GNSS fix: few satellites, or the HAL reports a network/cell-based position as GPS.
Fix after %1$s s, accuracy %2$s m, %3$d satellites used
Cold start: fix after %1$s s, accuracy %2$s m, %3$d satellites used
The GNSS HAL does not forward NMEA (gnssNmeaCb): apps that read NMEA (GPS testers, mapping and surveying tools) see nothing.
%1$d sentences have a wrong or missing checksum: the HAL corrupts or truncates NMEA.
The HAL advertises raw measurements and satellites are tracked, but no measurement arrived: the measurement interface of the GNSS HAL is broken.
Not supported by this HAL, or no satellite was tracked. Only needed by GNSS analysis apps.
Grant location access above to see satellites live.
Location is off, so the GNSS engine does not run. Turn it on to see satellites.
Every satellite has C/N0 = 0: the receiver is not getting RF (antenna/LNA path or RF configuration in the modem).
Signal but no fix after a minute: stay outside with open sky; without assistance data a cold start can take up to 12 minutes.
Centre = overhead, outer ring = horizon. Filled: used in fix; ring: not used; faded: no signal.
Carrier-to-noise density in dB-Hz; 30–45 outdoors is good.
Solid bars are used in the fix, faded ones are not; a red line means C/N0 = 0.
Commands sent to the GNSS provider; the engine decides what to do with them.
Deletes ephemeris, almanac, time and position cached by the engine, then restarts the TTFF timer. The next fix is slower; use it to measure a real cold start.
Asks the framework to fetch network time (NTP) and pass it to the engine. Needs a data connection.
Downloads predicted orbits (Qualcomm XTRA) from the server in gps.conf and injects them, which shortens the first fix to seconds. Needs a data connection.
